newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs underpinned by bank woes.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs underpinned by bank woes.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were underpinned by various news reports and rumours about the financial health of Japanese banks on Thursday.

But dealers said volumes were thin as players were cautious about taking aggressive positions after Tuesday's U.S. rate hike and ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey or tankan on April 2.
"I think the market is actually very jittery. It was moving up and down very quickly because of the thin volumes," said a dealer with a Japanese futures house.

News reports that Nippon Credit Bank was considering a restructuring caused confusion in the market, with talk the bank was going to withdraw from overseas operations and sell its Tokyo headquarters and Osaka office. A trader with a European futures house said JGB futures were sold on the back of reports the Japanese government planned to inject 90 billion yen into Nippon Credit Bank, sparking fears of further bond issues by the government.
But other traders shrugged off the reports as unlikely.
The bank issued a statement late on Thursday saying it was continuing to consider business improvement plans but nothing had been decided.
News of an appraisal loss of $50 million in derivatives trade at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd's U.S. unit also supported the market, dealers said.
"I see 99.10 as a resistance for December Euroyen. I'm still looking for a test of the lows of last week," the trader said.
"If the tankan comes out positive, we could see a lot of stop-loss selling. If December Euroyen breaks 98.95, we could see it another 10 ticks lower," he added.

The contract stood at 99.06 at 1120 GMT after fluctuating within an 11-point range against its IMM close at 99.05. June JGBs settled at 125.75 against their previous 125.88 after hitting a high of 126.26.
Eurodollar futures traded sluggishly but dealers said the market showed a bearish bias on expectations of another 25 basis point rate hike by the Federal Reserve in coming months.
September Eurodollars finished unchanged against their IMM close at 93.760 on volume of 7,525 lots.
